findings.failure_path: An inherited server with an auto-approved tool now remains enabled and available to the reviewer. A hostile diff or tool description can induce a remote write, send, or disclosure before audit_codex rejects the verdict. The read-only filesystem sandbox cannot prevent remote MCP effects, and rejection cannot undo them. Inherited descriptions can also influence the verdict without producing any forbidden tool-call event.
findings.smallest_fix: Exclude non-packet tool definitions and deny their invocation before execution, including plugin tools, while preserving selected skill loading. Keep the event audit as an additional check.

findings.failure_path: Substitution resistance remains an evidence gap. Finding one correctly named row with exact transport fields does not establish which implementation receives read_packet after inherited plugins register tools. The packet contains no resolution/dispatch implementation or adversarial trace covering colliding server/tool names. The new plugin_mcp fixture simply emits a passed verdict, so it would not detect a correctly advertised packet transport whose tool dispatch was substituted.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply inspectable dispatch evidence and a regression combining plugin inheritance with an actual packet read and a colliding or substituted packet-tool registration. Assert that only the frozen reader executes and that foreign-tool attempts cause no side effects.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Post-execution auditing cannot contain inherited tools. The predicate checks advertised transport fields, but the supplied packet does not establish substitution resistance during actual tool dispatch.

The CLI configuration widens available capabilities, while the new tests return canned verdicts without exercising containment. The extraction register consequently overstates the established boundary.

challenge_focus: Execution boundary: the preflight no longer disables inherited MCP servers, so they stay enabled during a packet-only review. Measured: a server that self-declares readOnlyHint is auto-approved and its tool executes; audit_codex only rejects the verdict afterwards. Attack the claim that this is an acceptable residual, and attack the preflight predicate itself for ways a mis-bound or substituted packet server passes it.
